Wikimedia Commons, “Saint Moses the Hungarian.jpg” — fetched 2026-08-28 at 450px wide. Artist as recorded there: Unknown monk. Date as recorded there: shortly after 1043. The licence is as Commons records it.

**Replaces the image this record carried until 2026-08-28.** That one was a modern painted icon with no recorded source, and its meta claimed copyright had expired — which cannot be true of a recent painting, because a living iconographer holds copyright in their own work as any painter does. The author asked on 2026-08-28 for pictures whose licence can actually be checked, so this one comes from Commons, where the provenance and the licence are recorded and linked rather than asserted here. That is what source_url is for: it is how a reader tests the claim instead of taking it on trust.
